forecast.event: first-release September 2026 U.S. CPI-U all-items seasonally adjusted month-over-month change is at least +0.4%

benchmarks.name: August_2026_no_change_point
benchmarks.note: Frozen prior-month headline CPI m/m value; simple no-change point benchmark.

benchmarks.name: neutral_binary
benchmarks.note: Protocol comparator only; not an empirical base rate.

resolution_rule: Use the first Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI news release for September 2026, scheduled for October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET. Resolve TRUE if the seasonally adjusted all-items CPI-U month-over-month percent change printed in that first release is >= +0.4%; otherwise FALSE. Score p=0.66 with Brier and log loss. Score the 0.5% point by absolute error against the first-release value and record whether the 0.1%-0.9% 80% interval covers. Compare the point with the frozen August no-change value of 0.4% and the probability with neutral 0.50. Do not retrofit a later economist consensus, energy-price path, revision, or post-cutoff forecast information.
rationale: September entered with an already-elevated inflation state: August headline CPI was +0.4% m/m and core CPI +0.3% m/m.

By the forecast cutoff, oil remained above $100 per barrel and U.S. diesel prices were at record levels; Reuters reported continued severe Hormuz impairment and Saudi Red Sea export disruption, giving the lagged retail-energy/input-cost channel a concrete September exposure.

The probability is capped well below certainty because oil retreated late in the week, Saudi Arabia is expanding Gulf/Oman rerouting and pursuing a partial East-West pipeline restart, CPI gasoline seasonal adjustment can differ from spot-price intuition, and core/shelter components may offset part of the energy impulse.
This forecast is intended to test the existing commodity-shock-to-measured-inflation pathway rather than infer the broader H003 regime from market prices alone.
surprising_if: Headline CPI is <= +0.1% m/m despite sustained September retail-fuel pressure; that would materially weaken the model's near-term energy pass-through calibration.
Headline CPI is >= +0.8% m/m and the acceleration is not narrowly confined to one volatile component; that would indicate stronger pass-through than the current state assumes.
source_notes: BLS states that September 2026 CPI is scheduled for October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET.

Reuters September 18 reporting: Brent and WTI remained above $100, Hormuz commodity-vessel traffic remained far below its recent average, and Saudi East-West/Yanbu disruption persisted alongside mitigation efforts.
Reuters September 18 reporting: EIA national diesel averaged $6.29/gal this week, 68% above a year earlier, with documented farm/freight cost pressure.
